outcome_definition.metric_implementation: pinder.eval.dockq (CLI: pinder_eval); DockQ computed as (Fnat + 1/(1+(iRMS/1.5)^2) + 1/(1+(LRMS/8.5)^2))/3 in src/pinder-eval/pinder/eval/dockq/metrics.py at the pinned commit
outcome_definition.acceptance_convention: DockQ >= 0.23 defines an acceptable-quality prediction (standard benchmark convention, stated in brief.md). The repository's own capri_class() classifies Acceptable/Medium/High from Fnat, iRMS and LRMS thresholds (metrics.py lines ~237-276) rather than from a DockQ cut-off; the 0.23 cut-off is the convention recorded in the brief, not a value found in the repository source.
reported_outcomes: DockQ / CAPRI class of the top-ranked pose
DockQ / CAPRI class of the best pose among a fixed number of generated candidates
wall-clock time, search throughput, time to an acceptable pose

stock_cuda_image_feasibility.reason: Unknown pending reproduction. Evidence for feasibility: the published environment (docker/frodock/Dockerfile.frodock) needs only OS packages (openmpi, fftw3, hdf5, gcc, build-essential) plus a pip install of the pinder package (requires-python >= 3.10; deps include torch, biotite<1.7, numpy<2, pyarrow, torch_geometric), all obtainable on a stock CUDA image; FroDock ships prebuilt linux64 binaries and a compile_frodock.sh. Evidence against assuming feasibility: the published base image is mambaorg/micromamba:1.5-jammy, not a CUDA image; brief.md records that the mirror README lists gcc 7.3.0 / Intel 18 and that 'compatibility, rebuilding and equivalence of compiled/prebuilt executables were not measured'; compile_frodock.sh prints a FRODOCK-2.0 banner while README utility versions differ. GPU is not required by the FroDock baseline (CPU + MPI).

size.download_basis: sum of all 3,602 inventoried inputs in brief.md (AAV mmCIFs, FroDock mirror archive, index.parquet, metadata.parquet, manifests, test_set_pdbs.zip, 3,590 individual structural/mapping files, source archive)
size.working_set_basis: test_set_pdbs.zip expands to 730,945,215 uncompressed bytes (0.68 GiB), FroDock archive expands to 65,507,120 bytes (0.061 GiB), plus FroDock grid/potential maps and decoy PDBs per docking run (tens of MiB per case) and in-memory index/metadata parquet (~0.3 GiB)
size.note: The complete PINDER release is ~1.04 TB (README.md line 18), but the full training set and bulk PDB/mapping ZIPs are not required for PINDER-S evaluation; brief.md records the same scoping.

scoring_and_repeatability.scoring_interface: pinder_eval --eval_dir <dir> [--method_name <name>] [--allow_missing] [--max_workers N]; eval_dir layout is <method>/<pinder_id>/{holo_decoys,apo_decoys,predicted_decoys}/model_<rank>.pdb, each decoy with exactly two chains R and L (README.md evaluation harness section)
scoring_and_repeatability.rank_extraction: decoy rank parsed with regex r"\d+(?=\D*$)" in pinder.eval.dockq.MethodMetrics
scoring_and_repeatability.determinism: not established. FroDock's FFT-based search is deterministic for fixed inputs and parameters in principle, but this was not measured; MPI rank count may affect clustering/ordering. The DockQ evaluation itself is deterministic given fixed decoys.
repeatability_rules: Use a fixed, preregistered selection of benchmark cases and independent random seeds (brief.md)
Report top-ranked pose and best-of-N separately; do not conflate search coverage with ranking quality (brief.md)
Record mpi_np, n_solutions and all FroDock stage parameters with results; the published adapter hard-codes the stage commands in src/pinder-methods/pinder/methods/run/frodock/predict.py
Material-identity caveat: the FroDock bytes are an unverified mirror; agreement with published-value anchors does not establish identity with the study's software (brief.md, Materials)

search_candidates.reason: The brief names a single benchmark (PINDER-S) with an executable published code path; no benchmark search was required and no substitute was considered.
